# IOC Extractor 0.3.0

[Русская версия](ru/v0.3.0.md)

Candidate notes for the 0.3.0 engineering release. Final source, artifact and
stand qualification remain subject to the release gate; this document is not a
publication or deployment receipt.

## Highlights

- Lifecycle-managed canonical SQLite data: fixed validity, active-only reads,
  typed history and bounded reconciliation.
- Stable sparse reusable IDs for immutable exports, separate from canonical IDs.
- Contract-driven local/SMB CSV import with atomic cross-artifact promotion and
  durable commit receipts.
- A standalone aggregate feed for IPv4, URL, FQDN and hashes.
- Required document/processed-import routing plans, disk-backed preparation and
  streamed source processing. Resource qualification remains workload-specific.
- Six reusable Java 21 library artifacts with independent publication records.

## Added

- Managed `as-is` and `processed` CSV intake with source/authority/contract
  catalogs, active-only matching, preview, status, replay and terminal retention.
  See [managed import](../../docs/guides/dataframe-import.md).
- `IOC_aggregate_generated.csv` and the separate `ioc-aggregate` export profile.
  Registered observation order, rather than completion order, controls mutable
  nonempty source names. See [aggregate usage](../../docs/guides/ioc-aggregate.md).
- Declarative named plans for document and processed-import preparation, including
  branch selection and independent resource limits. See
  [processing routes](../../docs/guides/ioc-processing-routes.md) and
  [resource sizing](../../docs/guides/bulk-resource-sizing.md).
- Published `io.github.xorex-lc` artifacts at `0.3.0-rc.1`:
  `ioc-platform-concurrency`, `ioc-platform-diagnostics-api`,
  `ioc-platform-logging-slf4j`, `ioc-config-spring-boot`, `ioc-platform-events`
  and `ioc-events-spring`. The [library catalog](../../docs/guides/libraries/README.md)
  links API/dependency/ownership guides and executable examples;
  [component records](README.md#maintain-library-records) retain original signed
  files, publication/recovery and separate repository consumers. Configuration's
  protected Central CI recovery remains TOOL-8; the two events artifacts require
  exactly matching versions and core-first qualification.

## Changed

- Dataframe schema advances to **v12**, service schema to **v14**. Migrations add
  lifecycle/identity/slots, managed-import receipts and accepted warnings,
  observation/provenance order, processing-policy pins, profile-scoped export
  exclusion and durable document execution admission.
- Production document processing uses owned disk workspaces and streaming
  HTML/DOCX paths. Preparation remains separate from canonical promotion; configured
  source/workspace/execution budgets must fit the selected workload.
- Canonical IDs and lifecycle IDs remain internal and non-reusable. Immutable
  export IDs are profile/artifact-scoped sparse reusable slots; surviving rows
  retain slots without compaction.
- Fresh production templates enable fixed 12-hour validity. Existing operator
  configuration is preserved and requires explicit lifecycle cutover.
- `address_blacklist` and `hashes` use compound record identity, preserving their
  public CSV shapes. Canonical truth remains embedded Native SQLite; the isolated
  alternative-storage experiment concluded without production activation.
- CSV output supports explicit LF/CRLF and independent header/data quoting.
  Defaults preserve CRLF/ALL/ALL bytes; changed layouts use versioned manifests.
  See [CSV format](../../docs/dev/csv-output-format.md).
- SMB encryption uses `required|preferred|disabled`; secure default requires an
  effectively encrypted SMB3 session before share I/O. Optional TCP `port`
  accepts `1..65535`, default 445, including managed import and change notifications.
- IOC logging delegates generic records, MDC restoration and lexical masking to
  the SLF4J library. Service catalogs, diagnostic disclosure and backend remain
  IOC-owned. Local event types use `ioc.event.type`; skipped operations use
  `ioc.operation.disposition=skipped` and omit inapplicable ECS classification.
- Independent library versions are accepted policy; Maven/CI activation remains
  TOOL-9. Current source versions remain lockstep.

## Fixed

- Bounded lifecycle deadline/projection/history recovery and revision-significant
  export: a newer lifecycle can require delivery even when CSV bytes are unchanged.
- Managed import uses one canonical promotion transaction and a dataframe commit
  receipt to recover completion without applying the delivery twice.
- Controlled configuration reports omit rejected values, parser/default exception
  text and unsafe dynamic paths. Indexed `spring.main.sources` is rejected before
  extra beans are created; the short-lived checker owns its lifecycle flags.
- Diagnostic suppression reporting retains the original failure when delivery
  throws the same exception instance again.
- Logging corrects ECS type/Throwable collisions; the Spring event adapter preserves
  wrapped Error identity and primary publication failure. Publication tooling rejects
  symbolic manifest/repository/artifact/recovery paths. Component records retain
  the exact release and regression scope of those fixes.

## Upgrade notes

1. Stop intake and optional remote work, then stop the service. Retain a coordinated
   rollback point: matching binary, operator YAML/environment, systemd unit/helpers,
   both SQLite databases and relevant service-owned files, exports and projections.
   Use the [deployment backup procedure](../../docs/guides/deployment.md); an ordinary
   copy of a live SQLite DB is not a consistent backup.
2. Upgrade a marked 0.2.0+ installation with managed import disabled. Validate both
   databases and reconcile the template explicitly. An old 0.1.0 installation
   retains its fresh side-by-side transition requirement.
3. For an existing dataframe DB, activate fixed validity only using the documented
   [two-restart cutover](../../docs/guides/canonical-record-lifecycle.md).
   `existing-records: expire` deliberately expires legacy active rows; `ttl=0`
   is not a migration command.
4. Review named processing plans, whole-list overrides, resource budgets and export
   profiles. Preview each import source/authority/contract before enabling intake.
   Import requires daemon mode, both JDBC stores and active fixed validity.
5. Aggregate starts empty, without historical backfill. Newly accepted document/
   oneshot observations and explicitly configured aggregate imports populate it.

Rollback after schema migration, lifecycle activation or accepted 0.3.0 writes
requires the complete matching pre-upgrade recovery point. Older code must not
open upgraded live databases. Deployment automation restores only its documented
scope; reconcile configuration, input movement and remote side effects separately.

## Breaking or observable contract changes

- Fixed validity changes active membership and introduces a one-way activation
  boundary. Export slots are not canonical identity; consumers must retain
  slice/profile/artifact context.
- Required processing plans and explicit resource admission can reject work that
  previously ran without those bounds. A large-workload success does not qualify
  smaller defaults, other document shapes or concurrent workloads.
- CSV line-ending/quoting changes affect bytes and manifest layout versions.
  Lossless encoding is required for immutable exports and MINIMAL/NONE projections;
  replacement in legacy ALL/ALL projections reports degraded completion.
- Temporary `ioc.sync.endpoints[].smb.encrypt` rollback alias remains accepted:
  `true` maps to required, `false` to disabled, with a value-free warning. New
  configuration uses `encryption`; supplying both keys is rejected.
- `ioc_aggregate` column order is exactly
  `name;ip_address;url_match;host_match;hash`. Each initial row carries one IOC;
  multi-carrier correlation is outside this release.
- Nested ECS JSON and strict `ioc.*`/`IOC_*` validation were established in 0.2.0.
  Keep that migration when upgrading from older installations. New logging field
  changes above require corresponding query/dashboard review.

## Known issues

Review the [current registry](../../docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md) before promotion. In particular:

- **ING-11/ING-13:** partial-run resume and pre-claim source disposition remain
  incomplete. Preserve original file/token evidence and use coordinated recovery;
  manual ledger edits are not a supported requeue procedure.
- **OUT-3/OPS-14:** lifecycle mapped-key collisions can reject a batch; whitespace-only
  imported ordered fields can bypass their intended guard. Use the documented
  configuration/input restrictions and aggregate/import mitigations.
- **OPS-10/OPS-11/OPS-12:** import status can fail on a NULL retry deadline; fetch
  identity lacks source/endpoint namespace and concurrent landing can overwrite
  an input. Use non-overlapping remote paths/names and coordinate inbox writers;
  periodic reconcile cannot repair these identity/ownership defects.
- **OPS-13/OPS-15:** failed activation preflight can leave mismatched host files;
  abnormal migration failure can leave partial DDL. Inspect and restore the
  matching unit/helpers or coordinated DB backup before restart/retry.
- **SRC-2/SRC-3, ING-15/ING-16, OUT-4:** parser-wide bounds, runtime advisory
  disposition, complete-cycle capacity/clock evidence and selected-processing
  budgets retain open qualification. Healthy startup is not acceptance of these scopes.
- **OPS-8:** historical Samba evidence does not qualify every target or the later
  two-identity SMB import contract. Keep a source disabled until qualified.
  **TOOL-10/TOOL-11** also limit lifecycle harness completion and local-deploy
  source-content evidence; see their recorded dispositions.

## Verification

Dated results, original failures, exact binary/configuration identities and
qualification limits are retained in the [qualification record](../release-evidence/0.3.0.md).
They are historical evidence, not fresh passes for the final candidate.

The selected release needs current reactor/analyzer/documentation checks,
applicable dependency/security disposition, packaged CLI/runtime checks,
fresh/upgrade/rollback and representative resource qualification. Preserve
named external skips and open blockers; unavailable checks are not passes.
Required SMB encryption needs its live policy contract, independently of earlier
file-operation evidence. Final source, digest and stand results must identify
the exact promoted bundle before publication.
